h1: Interior signs for New York spaces
lead: Interior signs shape the experience after someone walks through the door. A reception logo establishes identity, a directory explains the building and room signs make the last few steps easier. For New York offices, shops and shared properties, these elements work best as a coordinated system rather than isolated purchases. Vision Graphics helps frame the choices around your brand, the people using the space and the surfaces available. Begin with the areas visitors encounter first, then plan a consistent approach for the rest.

sections.h2: Build a readable family of signs
sections.html: Choose a hierarchy for building, floor, department and room information. Repeating type, colors and mounting details can make different sign formats feel connected without making every message equally prominent. Distinguish brand expression from navigation so decorative graphics do not compete with essential directions.

Photograph walls in ordinary lighting and note paint, texture, glass and existing fixings. A reception wall may suit dimensional letters, while changeable tenant information may need a panel system. Review landlord requirements and any accessibility-related design criteria with the responsible project team before selecting production details.

items.p: Individual letters and logos create depth on reception or feature walls.
Vinyl elements carry names, imagery and messages across suitable interior surfaces.
Coordinated panels organize identification and information that may change.

items.q: Should every room use the same sign?
items.a_html: Use a shared visual system, but let each sign’s purpose determine its size, content and any required tactile features.
Photos and a location list help identify what can remain and where replacement or additional signs would improve consistency.
